Daniel Mays, Joel Fry and Amit Shah star in a survival dramedy set in the breathtaking yet unforgiving Scottish Highlands. Lou (Mays), Dev (Shah), and Alistair (Fry), three old friends clinging to their annual wild camping tradition, begin their trip with banter, nostalgia, and amateur vlogging, but soon unravel into a battle of egos, secrets, and survival when they get lost, food runs short, and friendships fracture. At once funny, poignant, and unsettling, Wild explores the line between adventure and recklessness, and how toxic masculinity has become a huge part of the epidemic decline in men's mental health. Writer: Lewis Wren; Dir: BRICK; Vertigo Films

programme.title: Call the Bailiffs: Time to Pay Up!
programme.desc: Specialist Enforcement Agent Lewis faces a debtor named on a High Court writ for tens of thousands in unpaid commercial rent. When friends arrive and appear intent on interfering, Lewis must draw on his experience, legal knowledge and calm approach to stay in control. Meanwhile, Mark returns to a dry cleaner to recover money owed to two former employees, while Joe and Steve tackle a substantial debt at a money exchange business where funds are claimed to be unavailable. Series Prod: Katie Elliott; Senior Prod/Dir: Anna Lumsden; Exec Prods: Andrew Eastel/David Sumnall; Prod/Dir: John Russell; Northern Child (S4 Ep6)

programme.title: Murder Scene: The Incident Room
programme.desc: The Incident Room is the place where Britain's toughest murder cases are cracked. Behind closed doors, detectives work against the clock, piecing together the clues, chasing down suspects and searching for the breakthrough that will bring a killer to justice. Christmas Eve 2022: a packed pub, a burst of gunfire. Within seconds, six people are shot outside the Lighthouse Pub in Wallasey. Twenty-six-year-old Elle Edwards dies at the scene. A gunman armed with a military-grade machine gun has opened fire on innocent bystanders - and he's still out there. CCTV reveals this was no random act. As pressure mounts, a crucial breakthrough changes the direction of the case, triggering a nationwide manhunt for a dangerous and desperate fugitive. This is the story of a community shattered, a family devastated, and the relentless pursuit of a killer who believed he could disappear into the night. Exec Prods: Andrew Sheldon/Christian Hills; Dir: Luke Rufo; True North
Inside the nerve centre of murder inquiries, revealed through the detectives themselves.

programme.title: Cause of Death
programme.desc: Cause of Death returns with renowned forensic pathologist Dr Richard Shepherd. With decades of frontline experience, he reexamines evidence behind headline-making tragedies and haunting lesser-known cases, revealing how science can provide much needed answers following a sudden death. Nineteen-year-old apprentice bricklayer Jay Slater disappeared in Tenerife on 17 June 2024 after walking alone in the mountains on the north of the island. An inquest ruled his death was a tragic accident, but two years later his mother Debbie Duncan still has unanswered questions. Now, for the first time, Debbie is taken through her son's postmortem by the man who carried it out - Dr Richard Shepherd. And in search of answers to her son's last hours, Debbie returns to Tenerife with Dr Shepherd to recreate Jay's last walk. Exec Prods: Zoe Callan/Annaliese Edwards/Anna Hall; Dir: Lee Chapman; Candour Productions (S4 Ep1)
It's a coroner's job to ensure that no one goes to their grave with questions unanswered.

programme.title: Under Suspicion: Tracie Andrews - Road Rage Killer
programme.desc: Starring Emma Rigby, and written and directed by Grant Armour, this is a gripping psychological crime thriller told through first-hand accounts, police records, archive transcripts, and reconstructed memories. In December 1996, Tracie Andrews walks into a police station in Worcestershire, the apparent traumatised victim and the sole witness to her fiancé Lee Harvey's murder on a dark country lane following what appears to be a terrifying road-rage attack. Tracie is injured, shaken, and desperate for justice. As the investigation unfolds, Tracie's image becomes inseparable from the story. Media attention explodes as headlines transform her into a blonde bombshell figure of public sympathy. But as detectives revisit timelines, cross-check statements, and test forensic evidence, doubt begins to creep in. Small inconsistencies grow harder to ignore. Slowly, the woman who entered the station as a witness finds herself at the centre of suspicion. Dir: Grant Armour; Exec Prods: Nat Lippiett/Dan Grabiner; Orchard Studios

programme.title: Play for Today
programme.desc: A sharp, heartfelt, witty comedy starring Phyllis Logan and Max Harwood. Barbara, a ferociously stubborn English grandmother who chains herself to her beloved cottage when it's threatened with demolition by high-speed train developers. Peter, the company's smooth, painfully polite liaison is dispatched to remove her - only to discover she's also his estranged grandmother. What follows is a gloriously awkward battle of wills: Barbara's weaponised stubbornness and talent for public protest versus Peter's frantic attempts to keep his corporate career (and dignity) intact. As their standoff snowballs into a small town circus of press, protestors, and well-meaning locals, both are forced to reckon with what 'home' really means. Writer: Samson Hawkins; Dir: Rhys Aaron Lewis; Vertigo Films
